jobs.title: County Mental Health Program Specialist 1 (Local Government) Planning & Development
jobs.description:
THE POSITION

Are you passionate about working in an environment that serves to help others? Join Washington County Behavioral Health & Developmental Services (BHDS) team as a County Mental Health Program Specialist 1-Planning & Development. This role offers an opportunity to make a positive impact on adult mental health services across the county. You will be part of an agency that values teamwork, improvement, and commitment to others. We offer a generous benefit package and a supportive work environment. This is a great opportunity to help the community and residents of Washington County.

DESCRIPTION OF WORK

This position supports the administration and coordination of adult and transition age mental health programs within Washington County. It focuses on program monitoring, evaluation, quality assurance, and collaboration with service providers. As a County Mental Health Program Specialist 1, Planning & Development, you will perform the following duties:

Compliance Monitoring: Monitor service providers for adherence to federal, state, and local mandates and guidelines
Service Oversight: Oversee assigned services and address needs as they arise
Documentation Management: Create reports and maintain records related to assigned duties
Committee Participation: Represent the program on designated committees and support related activities
Incident Management: Assist with incident documentation and follow up discussions with providers
Community Engagement: Attend trainings and outreach events to maintain knowledge and support program goals

Work Schedule and Additional Information:

Full-time employment
Work hours are 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM, Monday - Friday, with 30-minute lunch.
Telework: You will not have the option to telework in this position.
Salary:In some cases, the starting salary may be non-negotiable.
You will receive further communication regarding this position via email. Check your email, including spam/junk folders, for these notices.

Required Experience, Training & Eligibility

QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum Experience and Training Requirements:

Two years of professional level experience in the field of mental health; and a bachelor's degree; or
An equivalent combination of experience and training.

Other Requirements:

You must meet the PA residency requirement . For more information on ways to meet PA residency requirements, follow the link and click on Residency.

jobs.title: Outdoor Recreation and Interpretation Program Coordinator (Natural Resource Program Specialist 2)
jobs.description:
THE POSITION

Step into a role that makes Pennsylvania’s outdoor spaces come alive! As the Outdoor Recreation and Interpretation Program Coordinator for the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, you help people discover new ways to explore nature. You guide programs that build outdoor skills, strengthen partnerships, and support lifelong learning. This position is perfect for someone who enjoys motivating others and creating meaningful outdoor experiences.

DESCRIPTION OF WORK

This position guides the development, coordination, and evaluation of statewide outdoor recreation and environmental education programs. The work strengthens public engagement, supports field staff, and ensures high-quality learning experiences across many initiatives. As a Outdoor Recreation and Interpretation Program Coordinator, you will perform the following duties:

Program Leadership: Lead statewide coordination, development, and evaluation of outdoor recreation and environmental education programs
Training Support: Develop and deliver training sessions, workshops, and lesson plans for field personnel and educators
Partnership Coordination: Work with agencies, schools, and organizations to advance recreation and education initiatives
Content Development: Create educational materials, virtual programs, and informational resources for public use
Program Evaluation: Assess program effectiveness, review reports, and recommend improvements to statewide initiatives
Technical Guidance: Provide expert assistance, interpret policies, and support field staff with program needs

Interested in learning more? Additional details regarding this position can be found in the position description .

Join a team that safeguards the natural places people and wildlife depend on every day! The Ecological Program Specialist with the Pennsylvania Game Commission plays an important role in protecting wildlife and guiding responsible natural resource use. This position offers a chance to work across forests, wetlands, and open lands to support healthy habitats. The work is meaningful and supports conservation efforts that benefit people and wildlife across the state. It is a great role for someone who enjoys science, outdoor work, and teamwork!

This position supports statewide environmental and land management efforts that guide safe and responsible oil, gas, and mineral activities on State Game Lands. It helps protect wildlife, habitats, and natural resources through careful planning, evaluation, and coordination. As a Ecological Program specialist, you will perform the following duties:

Field Inspections: Conduct site reviews to check resource development activities and identify impacts to wildlife and habitats
Plan Evaluation: Review and assess construction and permit plans to reduce or prevent harm to species and ecosystems
Issue Investigation: Investigate and address environmental problems caused by oil or gas operations on State Game Lands
Data Management: Maintain lease records, agreements, spatial data, and other information used for program decisions
Collaboration: Work with regional staff and other partners to restore sites and support responsible resource development
Technical Guidance: Provide recommendations on regulations, environmental requirements, and protection of wildlife resources

DESCRIPTION OF WORK

This position supports statewide environmental and land management efforts that guide safe and responsible oil, gas, and mineral activities on State Game Lands. It helps protect wildlife, habitats, and natural resources through careful planning, evaluation, and coordination. As a Ecological Program specialist, you will perform the following duties:

Field Inspections: Conduct site reviews to check resource development activities and identify impacts to wildlife and habitats
Plan Evaluation: Review and assess construction and permit plans to reduce or prevent harm to species and ecosystems
Issue Investigation: Investigate and address environmental problems caused by oil or gas operations on State Game Lands
Data Management: Maintain lease records, agreements, spatial data, and other information used for program decisions
Collaboration: Work with regional staff and other partners to restore sites and support responsible resource development
Technical Guidance: Provide recommendations on regulations, environmental requirements, and protection of wildlife resources

QUALIFICATIONS

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE, TRAINING & ELIGIBILITY

Minimum Experience and Training Requirements:

One year of experience as a Wildlife Biologist 2 or Natural Resource Program Specialist 1 (Commonwealth job title or equivalent Federal Government job title, as determined by the Office of Administration); or
Three years of experience as a Forester (Commonwealth job title or equivalent Federal Government job title, as determined by the Office of Administration); or
Three years of professional experience in management of plant, wildlife, or natural resources and a bachelor's degree in biology, botany, ecology, environmental science, forestry, natural resources management, or a closely related field; or
An equivalent combination of experience and training.
